```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
knitr::knit_hooks$set(inline = function(x) {
  if (is.numeric(x)) x <- format(x, big.mark = ",")
  paste(x, collapse = ", ")
})
```

The Proteome Discoverer tool output has two columns that a conversion
specification can use as the intensity: `Intensity`, the precursor's signal at
the moment its MS/MS spectrum was taken, and `Precursor Area`, the area of its
elution peak. Both look plausible to a language model. This vignette shows a
conversion specification that chose `Intensity`, how to change it to
`Precursor Area`, and what the choice does to the differential abundance
analysis. The conversion specification and the results of the analysis were
obtained once and saved, so the vignette runs without a language model or the
full tool output.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(MSstatsConvertLLM)
library(data.table)
```

# The tool output

We use the Proteome Discoverer output of PXD005642, a controlled mixture in
which proteins are spiked in known amounts into a constant *E. coli*
background. We distribute the rows of the tool output that the model was
shown. The benchmark of the manuscript normalized the column names before
showing them to the model, replacing spaces and other characters by dots, and
the conversion specification uses these names.

```{r tool-output}
case <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "pd_case_study.rds",
                            package = "MSstatsConvertLLM"))
tool_output <- normalize_headers(case$tool_output)
tool_output[, .(Protein.Group.Accessions, Sequence, Charge, Intensity,
                Precursor.Area)]
```

# Inferring the conversion specification

`infer_specification()` sends the model the column names and the first
`r formals(infer_specification)$n_preview` rows of the tool output. We obtained
the saved conversion specification with the call below, using llama3.1-8b and
the constrained_v3 prompt, in the benchmark of the manuscript.

```{r infer-live, eval = FALSE}
specification <- infer_specification(tool_output, "llama3.1-8b",
                                     "constrained_v3", acquisition = "DDA")
```

Here, we read the saved conversion specification instead.

```{r infer-saved}
specification <- case$specification
as.data.frame(specification$mappings)[, c("field", "from", "confidence")]
```

# Checking the intensity column

The model chose `Intensity`. In the example rows, both `Intensity` and
`Precursor.Area` are positive numbers, so neither looks wrong on its own. They
do not measure the same quantity, though: their ratio changes from row to row.

```{r candidates}
tool_output[, .(Intensity, Precursor.Area,
                ratio = round(Precursor.Area / Intensity))]
```

`Intensity` is the precursor's signal at the moment its MS/MS spectrum was
taken, recorded for each match, while `Precursor Area` is the area of the
precursor's elution peak. The hand-written converter, `PDtoMSstatsFormat()`,
reads `Precursor Area` unless told otherwise.

```{r converter-default}
formals(MSstatsConvert::PDtoMSstatsFormat)$which.quantification
```

The converter can also read `Intensity`, so the gold standard of the benchmark
accepts it, and the benchmark counted this choice as correct.

```{r gold-standard}
GOLD_STANDARD$proteome_discoverer$Intensity
```

# Changing the conversion specification

The conversion specification lists the fields in a data frame, so you can
change the intensity column before converting. Check that the new column
exists in the tool output.

```{r fix}
fixed <- specification
fixed$mappings$from[fixed$mappings$field == "Intensity"] <- "Precursor.Area"
as.data.frame(fixed$mappings)[fixed$mappings$field == "Intensity",
                              c("field", "from")]
"Precursor.Area" %in% names(tool_output)
```

# Differential abundance results

We converted the full tool output with the hand-written converter, which
reads `Precursor Area`, and with the LLM-based converter and the model's
conversion specification, which reads `Intensity`. We then analyzed both with
MSstats, as below. The script `compare_pxd005642.R` in the GitHub repository
of the package runs these steps.

```{r analysis-live, eval = FALSE}
tool_output <- fread("ControlMixture_DDA_ProteomeDiscoverer_input.csv")
annotation <- fread("annotation.csv")

converted <- list(
  hand = MSstatsConvert::PDtoMSstatsFormat(tool_output,
                                           annotation = annotation),
  llm  = LLMtoMSstatsFormat(normalize_headers(tool_output),
                            annotation = annotation,
                            specification = specification))
processed <- lapply(converted, MSstats::dataProcess,
                    normalization = "equalizeMedians",
                    featureSubset = "topN", n_top_feature = 3)
# contrast: one row for each pair of mixtures in which every spiked protein
# changes in amount
compared <- lapply(processed, function(p) MSstats::groupComparison(contrast, p))
```

Here, we read the saved results instead. They have one row per protein and
comparison. For each converter, they give the adjusted p-value, `adjp_h` for
the hand-written converter and `adjp_l` for the LLM-based converter, and
whether the protein was called significant, `sig_h` and `sig_l`. `spiked`
marks the spiked proteins, whose amount changes in every comparison, and
`in_h` and `in_l` say whether each converter's results include the protein. A
protein that MSstats could not test, because one condition has no measurement,
is never called significant, whatever its adjusted p-value.

```{r results}
results <- case$results
head(results, 3)
```

For each comparison, the table below counts the proteins called significant
with each column, and the spiked proteins among them.

```{r counts}
counts <- results[, .(area             = sum(sig_h, na.rm = TRUE),
                      area_spiked      = sum(sig_h & spiked, na.rm = TRUE),
                      intensity        = sum(sig_l, na.rm = TRUE),
                      intensity_spiked = sum(sig_l & spiked, na.rm = TRUE)),
                  by = .(comparison = Label)]
counts
```

Over the `r nrow(counts)` comparisons, the hand-written converter, with
`Precursor Area`, calls `r sum(counts$area)` proteins significant,
`r sum(counts$area_spiked)` of them spiked. The LLM-based converter, with
`Intensity`, calls `r sum(counts$intensity)`, `r sum(counts$intensity_spiked)`
of them spiked. The choice of the column decides how much of the true change
the analysis finds.

The table below counts, for each comparison, the proteins that both
converters call significant and those that only one of them calls
significant.

```{r overlap}
overlap <- results[, {
  h <- sig_h %in% TRUE
  l <- sig_l %in% TRUE
  .(both = sum(h & l), area_only = sum(h & !l), intensity_only = sum(!h & l))
}, by = .(comparison = Label)]
overlap
```

Over the `r nrow(overlap)` comparisons, the two converters share
`r sum(overlap$both)` significant calls, while `r sum(overlap$area_only)` are
significant only with `Precursor Area` and `r sum(overlap$intensity_only)`
only with `Intensity`.

# What to check

- Which column the conversion specification reads as `Intensity`. In a
  Proteome Discoverer tool output, prefer `Precursor Area`, the area of the
  precursor's elution peak, to `Intensity`, its signal at the moment its
  MS/MS spectrum was taken.
- When the tool output has more than one intensity column, compare them on
  the example rows. Columns whose ratio changes from row to row measure
  different things, and choosing between them changes the results.
- When MSstatsConvert has a converter for the tool, compare the conversion
  specification with the columns that the converter reads by default. The
  converter's help page lists them as the defaults of its arguments, for
  example `which.quantification`, `which.proteinid` and `which.sequence` in
  `?PDtoMSstatsFormat`.
